apod.explanation: Don't judge a galaxy by its size. This Hubble image shows NGC 4449, a dwarf galaxy about a tenth the size of the Milky Way — yet dwarf galaxies are the most common type in the universe. NGC 4449 and similar dwarfs are missing more oxygen than models predict, suggesting their stellar winds and supernovae are surprisingly effective at blowing away oxygen and other heavy elements. These tiny galaxies may play a big role in spreading the building blocks of stars, planets and life throughout the universe.
apod.title: NGC 4449: Small Galaxy, Big Impact

breaking.fact: After hot October CPI, Goldman Sachs — the first of its peers to revise — now expects the Fed to raise rates by another 25 basis points in March 2027, with a March move more likely than one in January and a third hike possible in the December dot plot. The call follows Gov. Waller's warning that a 50bp December move is on the table if core inflation stays hot.
breaking.headline: Goldman Sachs: Fed hike cycle isn't over — another hike possible in March

breaking.fact: Federal prosecutors unsealed an indictment Tuesday charging three alleged Iran-backed operatives with plotting nearly 20 attacks on Jewish communities in Europe and the United States, including an attack on RAF Fairford air base in England, from which US bombers were withdrawn in September. The men are accused of acting for Kata'ib Hizballah and Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps.
breaking.headline: DOJ charges three Iran-backed operatives over nearly 20 plots in Europe and the US

items.body: ADNOC Logistics confirmed one of its vessels was damaged in an attack in the UAE's territorial waters on Nov 10, the state-run Wam agency reported. The Houthis claimed fresh strikes on Riyadh airport, pumping stations along the East-West pipeline and an Aramco facility in Abqaiq; Saudi Arabia confirmed a limited fire on the East-West pipeline in the Medina region on Nov 9. Aramco has been pumping about 4 million barrels a day of exports through the pipeline to bypass the strait.
items.headline: ADNOC tanker hit in UAE waters; Houthis claim fresh Riyadh strikes

items.body: Ten attacks on vessels in the Strait of Hormuz and surrounding waterways have been recorded so far in November, against 37 in October — the highest monthly total since the war began, per the Washington Institute. Verified video showed the Navig8 Messi on fire near Oman on Sunday, one of three tankers hit that day for using 'unauthorised routes,' and UKMTO reported another tanker struck northeast of Oman's Lima on Tuesday. Oil leaking from damaged tankers has reached Oman's shores, with spills also seen off the UAE; the IMO counts 130 incidents in the region since February, with at least 25 seafarers killed.
items.headline: November attacks already at 10 as oil reaches Omani shores

hormuz.stats: Traffic & shares (latest verified): AIS-visible commercial traffic is running about 8% of normal — 6.9 ships a day over the past week (18 tankers) against 84.8 before the crisis. EIA puts Hormuz oil flows at 4.9M bbl/day in Q2 2026, down from 21.6M in Q4 2025; the IEA estimates ~20M bbl/day transited in 2025, about a quarter of global seaborne oil trade. China takes ~42% and India ~13% of strait crude throughput; ~90% of Iran's oil exports go to China. The EIA warns vessel-tracking data have become less reliable during the conflict.

space.body: SpaceX published the full flight plan Tuesday for Friday's Starship Flight 15, targeted for a 75-minute window opening at 4:45 p.m. CT on Nov 13: catch the Super Heavy booster at the tower about 6.5 minutes after liftoff, deploy 26 Starlink V3 satellites, orbit 14 times over ~22 hours, then attempt the first catch of an orbital upper stage, with re-entry around 2:56 p.m. CT Saturday. The FAA license modification for the upper-stage return was still unsigned as of Tuesday.
space.headline: SpaceX releases Flight 15 plan; FAA sign-off still pending

space.body: NASA is altering its lunar spacesuit design because of Artemis IV schedule pressure, shifting approach to keep the overall lunar landing timeline intact. No new suit architecture details have been released yet. Artemis, restructured in February 2026 after Artemis II's crewed lunar flyby in April, now plans a crewed Earth-orbit test in mid-2027 and the first crewed landing since Apollo 17 on Artemis IV in 2028.
space.headline: NASA rethinks lunar spacesuit design under Artemis IV pressure

space.body: A Caltech–Northwestern team built a digital twin of JWST's NIRCam — Physics-based Learning for Imaging Planets (FLIP) — that subtracts host-star glare far better than conventional processing, lifting detection sensitivity 2 to 15 times and recovering an exoplanet previously hidden in existing Webb frames. The Nature paper appeared online Nov 4; ScienceDaily carried the result Nov 10.
space.headline: JWST digital twin uncovers a hidden exoplanet in old images

weekInBrief.body: Consumer prices rose 0.4% in October (vs 0.3% expected) and core 0.3% for a third straight month; BLS published no 12-month rate after the 2025 shutdown wiped out Oct 2025 data. A December hike is now near-certain, Gov. Waller floated a 50bp move, and Goldman Sachs — first among peers to revise — now sees another hike in March 2027.
weekInBrief.headline: Hot October CPI reprices the Fed path

weekInBrief.body: OpenAI's revenue reached $10 billion in the third quarter, up 50% over the past quarter, according to a Wall Street Journal report — but adjusted operating losses widened to $10.9 billion. The numbers landed the same week Google-backed Anthropic filed for a Nasdaq listing at a reported $1.4 trillion valuation.
weekInBrief.headline: OpenAI revenue hits $10B in Q3, up 50% — but losses widen

weekInBrief.body: CERN's LHCb experiment has reported evidence that the neutral Bd meson can decay into a muon-antimuon pair — a process predicted only about once in 10 billion beauty-particle decays. Data from 2024–25 after a detector upgrade reached 3.0 sigma, 3.2 combined with earlier data: evidence, not yet the 5-sigma bar for discovery. The rate agrees with the Standard Model so far.
weekInBrief.headline: LHCb finds first evidence of a one-in-10-billion particle decay

weekInBrief.body: Researchers at the University of Basel have identified and coherently controlled 'forbidden' vibrational transitions in single trapped nitrogen molecules — repeatable laser measurements that read the molecule's state without destroying it. Published in Nature Communications, the quantum-logic spectroscopy could sharpen molecular clocks and sensors.
weekInBrief.headline: Laser reveals 'forbidden' vibrations in single molecules
